lines: I.  Introduction
Fig. 2.  Fitted exponent minus the predicted 2r, over all 600 cells. On the asymptotic tail it is centred on zero; on the full grid it is biased low.

Two fixed worlds are to be told apart from observations. Rather than vary the worlds, we hold them fixed and vary the ADMISSIBLE MEASUREMENT. The observation density of world W at perturbation scale h is a finite Gaussian mixture:

Expanding in h produces coefficients Δ_j, and the LEAKAGE ORDER is the least j with Δ_j ≢ 0. Two things must be established separately, and the second is the one usually skipped: the coefficients below order r cancel, and Δ_r ≢ 0.

If the leakage order is a property of the query rather than of the parameter space, then an experimenter who cannot change the worlds can still change the rate, by changing what is legal to measure. The cost of doing so is what this work computes.
What the literature leaves open
The literature therefore leaves a specific opening.

No existing treatment simultaneously: (i) attributes the leakage order to the admissible measurement rather than the parameter space; (ii) proves non-vanishing for shifted Hermite sums instead of assuming it; (iii) gives a sandwich whose two sides share the exponent and whose constants are both written down; and (iv) certifies that the normalised ratio has a positive limit, so that two measurements are compared through genuine leading terms rather than envelopes.
II.  Methodology
Every statement displayed below is machine-checked, with no unproved step anywhere in the chain.  STEP 1 — THE GAUSSIAN DERIVATIVES, BUILT  (C2).
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Induction on n, with the derivative of a polynomial times a Gaussian computed by the product rule at each step.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Via the multilinear iterated derivative and the fact that iteratedDeriv is that object applied to the all-ones vector; smoothness of each component.
STEP 3 — NON-VANISHING, THE HARD HALF  (C2).
WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM STEP 2. Step 2 gives the coefficient as a level sum; Step 3 shows that sum is not identically zero.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Factor the Gaussian and divide by the largest level's factor.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  The lower side is a Cauchy–Schwarz interval bound: an inequality holding for every t > 0 is converted into a quadratic bound on H².
This converts the sandwich on H² into a sandwich on the per-sample log-affinity L = −log(1−H²), at the cost of a factor 2.
STEP 6 — MATCHING SAMPLE COMPLEXITY  (C4).
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Exponentiating the per-sample bound and comparing with the target error; ceil_suffices states that the integer ceiling suffices.
with γ = 13983/32768 and L_max = 2401/4096, both exact rationals read off the loss geometry.
STEP 8 — THE ANALYTIC LIMIT  (C5).
WHY THIS IS NEEDED. A sandwich localises the ratio in an interval; it does not say the ratio converges, nor identify the limit.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Dominated convergence along h ↓ 0, with the envelope of Step 4 as the dominating function; positivity of the limit follows because a non-negative.
III.  Results

THE MEASURED REGRET LANDS INSIDE THE PROVED WINDOW. Two admissible measurements of the SAME pair of worlds were simulated with 4000 repetitions per world. The order-2 measurement needs N = 4,678 samples and shows mean regret 0.008353; the order-1 measurement needs N = 41,006 and shows 0.009159.
The ratio 41,006 / 4,678 ≈ 8.8 is not a property of the worlds — they are identical in both runs — but of which measurement was admissible.
IV.  Discussion

THE EXPONENT IS 2r ON INSTANCES NOBODY CHOSE. Two hundred instances were drawn and a perturbation of designed order 1, 2 or 3 built on each from a Prouhet–Thue–Morse pair; the order was then recomputed from the level coefficients and matched the design in all 600 cells.

Carried to orders four and five, order four is as clean; order five is at the double-precision floor, and is reported with a reliability flag fixed before the run rather than quietly. THE FIT WINDOW IS NOT A DETAIL.

An analyst fitting the full range concludes a high-order query is better than it is, by a margin that grows exactly where the claim is largest. WHAT THE ORDER DOES NOT CONTROL. At a fixed h the sample counts do not order by leakage order: medians 527, 1095, 883 at orders 1, 2, 3.
Limitations — what is not established
Fig. 3.  The assembled coefficient as the top-level gap closes. All three orders fall at slope one over three decades, and no cell reached zero at a positive gap.

Ties at the top are not covered. Theorem needs the largest level carrying a non-zero coefficient to be strictly largest. When two levels tie, the exponential factors no longer separate and the argument gives 0=0.

Section measures the approach: the coefficient degenerates linearly in the gap and never vanishes at a positive one, so the hypothesis is essential and cannot simply be dropped, but nothing discontinuous happens at the tie either. The window does not close.

The paired comparison still uses two measurements, not a family. Experiment~E2 supplies the family for the rate — six hundred cells at three orders, with the exponent fitted rather than assumed — but its instances are independent draws, so it cannot pair.

What E2 adds, and what Section reports, is that the sample counts do not order by leakage order at a fixed h at all: the paired factor is a statement about one pair of measurements at one scale, and generalising it to “higher order costs more samples” is not supported.

The asymptotic statements hold as h0, and at the simulated scale h=0.6 the remainder terms suppressed in Theorem are not negligible — which is why the per-sample H^2 is computed exactly there rather than from the envelope.

The asymptotic regime is therefore computed, never observed. Nothing here is minimax. Every result concerns a fixed pair and a fixed query, and the dropped normalisation means the displayed expressions are not densities.
V.  Conclusions
Fig. 1.  Squared Hellinger distance between two worlds sharing a level set. The three groups are fans of slope 2r and do not cross.

Which query you are allowed to ask, not how many samples you take, sets the rate. The order-r coefficient is proved non-vanishing, the Hellinger sandwich pins the exponent at 2r from both sides, and 600 drawn instances reproduce that exponent to within 0.034.
A tied case would need a different statement, not a stronger one.
How the numbers were produced

THE ORDER IS BUILT, THEN VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. Each instance is constructed to have a chosen leakage order; the order is then recomputed from the level coefficients by the procedure the paper proves, and compared. A cell whose top level ties is reported undetermined rather than counted.

The second forced the level moments to vanish — which is impossible for positive weights at order 2, so order 3 was unreachable, and 600 cells came back order 1 again. Both errors came from modelling ONE world; the paper's definition compares TWO.
